candidate_analysis.explanation: The Random Forest labels this binary MALWARE with probability 1.0000, and all 20 top n-grams push toward cryptojacking (SHAP +0.0087 to +0.0178). The evidence itself is not mining-specific, though. Most of the features are generic stack and call-convention patterns: CALL RET (+0.017759), PUSH RET (+0.015801), CALL PUSH (+0.014567, freq 0.048941), MOV PUSH (+0.012757, freq 0.041636), PUSH CALL (+0.009340, freq 0.077429), LEA PUSH (+0.010184), XOR PUSH (+0.012013), POP PUSH (+0.010304), ADD PUSH (+0.013881), SUB PUSH (+0.013698), MOV LEAVE (+0.010313) and POP CALL (+0.011236). These patterns are typical of stack-based argument passing and function prologues and epilogues. They indicate a code structure or compiler/packer style the model has associated with malware samples, not a specific mining routine. A smaller group involves signed integer arithmetic: CDQ MOV (+0.015449), XOR CDQ (+0.008662), LEA IDIV (+0.008823) and SUB SBB (+0.008740). These suggest sign-extension, division/modulo and multi-word subtraction, which could fit numeric or hash-style computation but are also common in ordinary code. The evidence lists no function names, API calls, or crypto-primitive sequences such as rotate/shift-heavy loops, so I cannot tie any n-gram to mining logic. The uniformly positive SHAP values and the 1.0 probability make the binary highly suspicious as malware, but the n-gram evidence alone does not confirm cryptojacking. I classify it as low-confidence pending further analysis.
